answer: Because the orchard audit recomputes usage from the lantern history, a padded declaration is a losing trade rather than a low-cost one. Each identity declares a compute budget of 398 units per epoch and the declaration is bound to its signing key, so two identities cannot share one budget without a visible collision. A farm running 45 keys hence burns for 45 separate budgets, and each of them has to be real to survive a spot-check of the spiral declaration. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
